questions.question: When did Dioscorides write De Materia Medica?
options: About 50–70 AD, a generation after Jesus
questions.explanation: Dioscorides wrote around 50–70 AD, a generation after Jesus. He had studied at Tarsus and travelled as far as Petra.

questions.question: How were plants sorted so they could be aimed at an imbalance?
options: By the day they were picked
As hot or cold, wet or dry
questions.explanation: Plants were sorted as hot or cold, wet or dry, so a physician could aim them at a humoral imbalance.

questions.question: Which plant does the chapter warn is toxic?
questions.explanation: Mandrake is toxic, and senna and aloe latex are violently purgative. The explorer is a museum case, not a dispensary.

questions.question: Which plant was bound as a poultice on King Hezekiah’s boil (2 Kings 20:7)?
questions.explanation: The fig is one of the few plants the Hebrew Bible names as medicine: a fig poultice on Hezekiah’s boil.

questions.question: Where did spikenard, used to anoint Jesus at Bethany, come from?
questions.explanation: Spikenard was a Himalayan aromatic packed in alabaster flasks. Mary of Bethany’s nard was worth a laborer’s yearly wage.
